messages:
Alex S: forwarding a customer escalation (ACME) — they say model outputs changed after last night's rollout, producing stale/mismatched completions for the same prompt. ticket: https://zendesk/acme/9876
Maria (CS): how bad is it? does it affect many users or a single endpoint? :eyes:
Alex S: affects 2 production routes (chat v2) in us-west and ap-southeast, customer reports ~40% of requests suddenly returning old canned answers that were removed in the previous model version. Happened ~2026-03-15 22:10 UTC after canary -> full rollout.
Alex S: example (redacted):
Customer prompt: "Generate onboarding checklist for finance team"
Response (expected): "...include data retention, access controls..."
Response (observed/stale): "...include deprecated billing flag X and legacy webhook config Y..."
Maria (CS): yikes. customer severity P1, they blocked on this. they requested immediate mitigation.
Jing (eng-runtime): tagging in. initial hypothesis: KV prefix cache serving entries from old model variant because prefix keys were not namespace-isolated during rollout. seeing similar pattern in previous regressions. Can you paste request_id or api logs?
Alex S: pasted request IDs and a short curl that reproduces on their account:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"chat-v2","prompt":"Generate onboarding checklist for finance team","prefix":"acme:template:v2"}'
Sam (eng-ml): putting forward another angle — during the rollout we swapped tokenizer normalization flag (normalize_whitespace=true) for performance. That changes tokenization boundaries and therefore the prefix hash used for KV keys. If the rollout mixed variants, old KV entries might be matched incorrectly or reused.
Jing (eng-runtime): checking cache telemetry now — I see a spike in KV hit rate at the time of rollout followed by a high rate of stale retrievals flagged by our canary monitors. Also found some prefix collisions where two variants shared a computed prefix key.
Jing (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations I can run:
- invalidate prefix cache for customer namespace (admin endpoint)
- temporarily set requests to bypass KV with header `x-kv-bypass: true`
- rollback normalization flag on model if needed
Maria (CS): customer asked for a hotfix now. which option is fastest with lowest blast radius?
Jing (eng-runtime): admin cache invalidation for the specific prefix is fastest. sequence:
1) call internal endpoint: POST /admin/cache/clear_prefix { "namespace": "acme", "prefix": "template:v2" }
2) set `x-kv-bypass: true` for their traffic for 30m to avoid re-populating with bad entries
3) monitor canary metrics + trace sampled requests
Sam (eng-ml): need to confirm whether cache key derivation changed between variants — if yes, we should rebuild/re-hash entries or perform a full customer-prefix eviction. I'll diff the model config.
Alex S: ran admin clear_prefix for acme template:v2 at 1865003000, customer says immediate improvement on ~30% of affected requests. they still see occasional stale responses.
Jing (eng-runtime): sounds like partial cleanup. There may be multiple prefixes (legacy names) or KV TTLs were extended. I'm running a sweep across their namespace now. giving ETA ~15m. ops-bot: kicked off cache-sweep job job_id=cache-sweep-1865003200
deploy-bot: canary->prod rollout for chat-v2 completed 02:05 UTC; note: changed tokenizer.normalization to true
Sam (eng-ml): confirmed tokenizer.normalization flip. That would change internal prefix hashing. If a portion of traffic hit old variant and populated shared cache keys, eviction has to cover both hashed forms.
Jing (eng-runtime): action list I propose:
- finish full prefix sweep for acme (in progress)
- short-term: set per-customer KV-bypass header for acme 30m
- mid-term: deploy a migration to append variant-id to cache namespace so keys are variant-isolated
- postmortem: root cause + checklist to avoid mixing key schemes in rollouts
Maria (CS): I've told ACME we're executing the cache sweep and will apply bypass. asking if we should schedule a short rollback window if this doesn't clear in 1 hour.
Alex S: customer prefers not to rollback if possible. asks for status updates every 15m.
Jing (eng-runtime): cache-sweep finished at 1865004200, removed ~12k entries for acme namespace, telemetry shows stale-hit rate dropping from 43% -> 4%. continuing to monitor.
Sam (eng-ml): also pushed a small patch to model-config to include `cache_key_version` and will coordinate with runtime to start writing new keys. this avoids future collisions.
Maria (CS): ACME confirms majority of requests now correct. they asked for a remediation plan doc and a dedicated postmortem.
Alex S: creating postmortem ticket and assigning owners: Jing (eng-runtime) lead, Sam (eng-ml) data root cause, Maria (CS) customer RCA and comms.
Jing (eng-runtime): final notes: mitigation timeline: invalidate prefix -> bypass -> sweep -> config change. recommend adding a pre-rollout check to assert cache key scheme unchanged when changing tokenizer/config flags.
Sam (eng-ml): will add unit test for cache key stability and flag-dependent key derivation in model onboarding repo.
Maria (CS): closing loop with customer and scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
